result.summary: This pull request adds an optional `precious` parameter to the `submitBlock` and `submitSolution` methods on the Mining IPC interface. When set, a submitted block with identical work to the current tip is marked as precious and activated atomically. It also refactors `Chainstate::ActivateBestChain` into an internal helper so `PreciousBlock` can perform the reorg and report tip status without releasing `m_chainstate_mutex`.
result.problem: External mining software using the IPC interface has no direct mechanism to indicate preference for a locally mined block over an existing same-work tip. Operators must resort to issuing a separate `preciousblock` RPC call, which is non-atomic and risks racing concurrent chainstate updates.

open_concerns: Sjors suggested that submitBlock should return 'duplicate' if the block was already known, even if precious is requested and the tip is reorged.
Sjors recommended splitting and reorganizing the unit test in miner_tests.cpp due to its size.

result.card: This pull request adds an optional precious parameter to the Mining IPC submitBlock and submitSolution methods, enabling mining clients to submit and prioritize a same-work block in a single IPC call. It also refactors Chainstate::PreciousBlock and ActivateBestChain to verify tip connection status atomically while holding the chainstate mutex. Reviewers agree with the concept, though questions remain about duplicate return semantics and test structure. The branch currently has merge conflicts and needs a rebase before code review can conclude.
